subject: huntsman spider
title: Scientists Raced 258 Spiders. The Winner Can Outrun a Jogger

scenes.text: There's a spider that could outrun you on a morning jog.
Scientists clocked two hundred and fifty-eight species. The winner: Australia's brown huntsman, about eight miles an hour.
A typical jogger manages four to six. The old record holder hit half that, and only by cartwheeling downhill.
The huntsman's secret is very long legs on a light, three gram body.
A fifty-two gram bird-eater managed under one mile an hour. So the spider that outruns you isn't the biggest.

description:
A study of 258 spider species from the University of Greifswald and Imperial College London found the fastest runner is Australia's brown huntsman (Heteropoda), with a top speed of about 3.6 metres per second, a little over 8 mph. A typical jogger does 4 to 6 mph.
The old record holder, the Moroccan flic-flac spider, reached about 3.8 mph by tumbling downhill, while a 52-gram salmon pink bird-eater moved under 1 mph. The results are a preprint and not yet peer reviewed.
Would you race a huntsman?
first_comment: Bonus: a goblin spider weighing a tenth of a milligram still hit almost half a mile an hour. Would you outrun a huntsman?
